evidenceStatus: Historical internal dispositions from 2026-08-16; not regenerated after ADR 0044, contains pre-ADR-0044 Mine symbols, and is not current-tree release evidence.

internal-protocol-security.name: GUM BALL 6900 protocol engineering
internal-protocol-security.role: Internal protocol security review; not an independent audit

rationales.slither:assembly: Reviewed EIP-1153 Fund duplicate-mark primitives use domain-separated keys and explicit success-path clearing; no arbitrary memory or storage access exists.
rationales.slither:calls-loop: Reported calls are in fixed-eight, scalar-escapable, caller-selected, or explicit convenience loops whose maximum gas and atomicity are documented.
rationales.slither:divide-before-multiply: Division followed by multiplication deliberately recovers the exactly indexed quotient while preserving the unindexed remainder in scaled carry state.
rationales.slither:incorrect-equality: Each equality is an exact empty-amount, zero-weight, or unchanged-index state-machine sentinel, not an access-control or probabilistic comparison.
rationales.slither:naming-convention: The underscore-delimited Resonance ledgers preserve the pinned Liquid Signal accounting vocabulary and their existing public getter ABI; the names do not affect storage isolation or authorization.
rationales.slither:redundant-statements: The named ERC-721 receiver parameters are deliberately ignored while retained in the generated ABI and NatSpec; authorization uses manager, depositor, token, pool, and custody state.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-balance: BribeRouter deliberately snapshots supported-token balances around a guarded call to prove exact deltas; nonReentrant prevents callbacks from making those baselines stale and transaction rollback preserves the fixed liability on failure.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-benign: Reported factory and Bribe callbacks are guarded, constructor-isolated, or occur before graph activation; no callback can retain a partially written authorized state.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-events: Reported events follow guarded factory or owner-only calls and do not expose a callback-reachable authorization or value-transfer boundary.
rationales.slither:reentrancy-no-eth: Reported token interactions occur beneath nonReentrant entry points with effects-first accounting and atomic rollback of every later index or epoch write.
rationales.slither:timestamp: Timestamps intentionally drive fixed emission epochs, seven-day reward streams, bounded reverse Dutch prices, and caller deadlines with tested boundary semantics.
rationales.slither:unused-return: The ignored convenience values are non-authoritative; typed downstream calls revert on failure and exact token deltas independently prove complete routing.
rationales.slither:weak-prng: Modulo is used only to retain deterministic fixed-point accounting carry; the protocol contains no random selection or entropy-dependent outcome.
rationales.aderyn:centralization-risk: Findings identify the intentionally minimal Resonance administration and its controlled factories; production deployment remains blocked until ownership is transferred to a separately reviewed external governance executor.
rationales.aderyn:costly-loop: Loops are capped at eight, caller-selected, incrementally bounded, or paired with scalar alternatives; worst-case gas is measured against the pinned chain limit.
rationales.aderyn:large-numeric-literal: Reported values are named fixed supply, emission, precision, fee, price, or time constants pinned by tests and independent economic fixtures.
rationales.aderyn:literal-instead-of-constant: The two literals are fixed positions in the pinned PositionManager return tuple and are tested against canonical pool and position identity.
rationales.aderyn:local-variable-shadowing: Reported constructor parameters and local currency values are explicitly qualified or scoped and compile to unambiguous immutable assignments.
rationales.aderyn:modifier-used-only-once: The single-use onlyResonanceRouter modifier is retained as the named authorization boundary for revenue notification; it performs only a sender comparison and cannot call out or mutate state.
rationales.aderyn:redundant-statement: ERC-721 operator and data are intentionally ignored but named for ABI and NatSpec clarity; neither is an authorization input.
rationales.aderyn:reentrancy-state-change: Every reported state transition is constructor-isolated or beneath nonReentrant checks-effects-interactions with exact-delta verification and adversarial rollback tests.
rationales.aderyn:require-revert-in-loop: Batch and selected-token operations intentionally revert atomically; fixed-eight and caller-selected loops retain scalar or omission paths for broken tokens.
rationales.aderyn:state-variable-could-be-immutable: Resonance.rewardTokens is a dynamic storage array initialized once with USDG; Solidity immutable variables cannot use dynamic array types, and the array preserves the reviewed Bribe-shaped enumeration API.
rationales.aderyn:storage-array-memory-edit: Mine._price intentionally accepts a read-only memory snapshot so both the replacement path's prior-slot copy and the public price view can share identical auction arithmetic; no caller expects it to update storage.
rationales.aderyn:unchecked-return: Reported returns are convenience values or revert-only typed validations; authoritative completion is enforced by revert and exact observed token deltas.
rationales.aderyn:uninitialized-local-variable: The reported loop index intentionally uses Solidity value-type zero initialization and is never populated from or confused with external state.
rationales.aderyn:unused-public-function: Reported functions are intentional public preview, accounting, pool-key, and custody APIs used by offchain consumers and permissionless monitoring.

canonical-ledger-names.impact: Renaming a public accounting ledger would change the generated ABI and could make integrations or independent monitors query the wrong compatibility surface.
canonical-ledger-names.exploitability: The finding is purely lexical: each underscore-delimited mapping retains normal Solidity key isolation and is written only through the same guarded reward-checkpoint paths as its mixed-case peers.
affectedAssumptions: The retained Liquid Signal ledger names remain deliberate public compatibility and review vocabulary.
No authorization decision depends on parsing or comparing variable names.
canonical-ledger-names.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a reported ledger is renamed, its visibility changes, or its read/write authority changes.
compensatingControls: Generated ABI checks pin public getter names and result shapes.
Reward conservation tests and invariants exercise every reported ledger independently of source naming.

named-revenue-authorization.impact: Weakening or obscuring the revenue-source check could let an arbitrary caller restart the global USDG schedule or make Resonance pull from an unintended account.
named-revenue-authorization.exploitability: The reported modifier performs one equality check against the one-time-bound ResonanceRouter and makes no external call or state change; retaining it makes the sole revenue authorization boundary explicit even though it currently has one call site.
affectedAssumptions: ResonanceRouter remains one-time-bound after reciprocal Resonance and USDG identity checks.
notifyRevenue remains the only entry point that can pull and schedule Resonance USDG.
named-revenue-authorization.revisitTrigger: Re-review if revenue notification gains another caller, the router binding changes, or the modifier gains interaction or state mutation.
compensatingControls: Authorization tests reject direct notification by every caller other than the bound Router.
Exact balance-delta checks prove that successful notifications pull the declared USDG amount from that Router.

read-only-slot-snapshot.impact: If auction quoting were expected to mutate a live slot, copying storage to memory could silently omit that state transition and misprice a replacement.
read-only-slot-snapshot.exploitability: _price is a view-only arithmetic helper and never writes its Slot argument; the replacement path deliberately quotes a previously copied Slot while the public price view copies the current storage Slot under normal Solidity memory conversion.
affectedAssumptions: Auction quoting remains a pure read of initialPrice and auctionStartedAt plus the current timestamp.
All slot mutations remain explicit in occupation, replacement, checkpoint, and capacity paths.
read-only-slot-snapshot.revisitTrigger: Re-review if _price stops being read-only, accepts additional mutable state, or participates in slot checkpointing.
compensatingControls: Boundary tests pin the start, hourly decay, terminal-zero, occupation, and replacement prices.
State-machine invariants reconcile every live slot after arbitrary checkpoints and replacements.

single-reward-storage-shape.impact: Unexpected mutation of Resonance reward-token membership could introduce an unreviewed revenue asset or make offchain enumeration disagree with the accounting ledger.
single-reward-storage-shape.exploitability: The finding targets a dynamic storage array, a type Solidity does not permit as immutable; the constructor appends exactly USDG and no post-construction function can append, replace, or remove an element.
affectedAssumptions: Resonance permanently schedules only its constructor-immutable USDG token.
getRewardTokens and the public array getter remain the reviewed single-token enumeration surface.
single-reward-storage-shape.revisitTrigger: Re-review if Resonance token registration, constructor initialization, or reward-token enumeration changes.
compensatingControls: Tests assert the sole reward token is USDG and reject forbidden reward-token administration.
Resonance exposes addBribeReward for Strategy Bribes but no owner method that mutates the Resonance reward token.

exact-carry-arithmetic.impact: Incorrect quotient or remainder handling could strand value, over-accrue liabilities, or make reward conservation depend on call cadence.
exact-carry-arithmetic.exploitability: The reported division and modulo operations implement quotient-and-remainder carry accounting, never randomness; every remainder is retained in explicit scaled state until it becomes distributable.
affectedAssumptions: Scaled pending, indexed, user, sole-signaler, and Fund carry remains included in the documented conservation equations.
Reward and revenue precision constants remain fixed and arithmetic remains checked.
exact-carry-arithmetic.revisitTrigger: Re-review whenever a precision, quotient, remainder destination, stream transition, checkpoint order, or conservation equation changes.
compensatingControls: Unit tests exercise sub-precision, sole-signaler, zero-supply, final-second, and repeated-checkpoint boundaries.
State-machine invariants reconcile every whole and scaled liability against exact supported-token balances.

exact-boundaries.impact: Changing an exact zero, identity, or index boundary could skip accounting work or route value to the wrong liability class.
exact-boundaries.exploitability: Each reported equality is a documented state-machine sentinel for an empty amount, unchanged index, zero signal weight, or Strategy settlement branch.
affectedAssumptions: Zero and equal-index states retain their documented accounting meanings.
exact-boundaries.revisitTrigger: Re-review if any reported sentinel, branch order, index transition, or zero-amount policy changes.
compensatingControls: Boundary tests cover zero, one-unit, unchanged-index, and neighboring state transitions.

transient-redemption-marks.impact: Incorrect transient-storage namespacing or clearing could admit duplicate redemption assets or couple independent redemptions in one transaction.
transient-redemption-marks.exploitability: The two assembly blocks contain only EIP-1153 tstore and tload for a domain-separated token key; every successful redemption clears each mark, while reverts discard transient state transactionally.
affectedAssumptions: Robinhood Chain continues to support EIP-1153 semantics used by Solidity 0.8.26.
The transient key domain and success-path clearing loop remain unchanged.
transient-redemption-marks.revisitTrigger: Re-review if the key derivation, selected-token validation order, clearing loop, compiler, or target EVM version changes.
compensatingControls: Tests cover duplicates in arbitrary order and multiple redemptions through one outer transaction.
Fund redemption remains nonReentrant and rejects zero address and GBX before any burn.

bounded-or-escapable-loops.impact: A caller-controlled external-call loop could make a required claim, redemption, or signal exit unavailable at practical chain gas limits.
bounded-or-escapable-loops.exploitability: Reward-token loops are capped at eight and have scalar or selective claim alternatives; account strategy loops have scalar signal mutation paths; redemption is caller-selected by design; settlement is explicitly bounded.
affectedAssumptions: Bribe reward registration remains capped at eight tokens in code.
Scalar claim, selective claim, incremental signal, and bounded epoch-settlement entry points remain available.
bounded-or-escapable-loops.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a cap rises, a scalar/range escape path is removed, a loop body gains interaction, or chain transaction gas limits fall materially.
compensatingControls: Maximum-eight-token gas tests measure entry, exit, claim, and acquisition paths against the live chain limit.
Atomic revert is intentional for caller-selected batches; broken tokens can be omitted through scalar or selective paths.

guarded-callback-ordering.impact: A genuine reentrancy ordering flaw could duplicate claims, corrupt signal weights, or expose a partially registered Strategy graph.
guarded-callback-ordering.exploitability: Reported value paths are nonReentrant; private functions inherit the active guard, constructor factory calls cannot reach a registered live graph, and state is advanced before supported-token interaction with atomic rollback.
affectedAssumptions: Every public value-moving entry point retains nonReentrant coverage.
Factories remain Resonance-controlled and deployed Strategies and Bribes retain immutable authorization links.
guarded-callback-ordering.revisitTrigger: Re-review on any external-call reordering, new callback-capable dependency, factory authorization change, or reentrancy-guard change.
compensatingControls: Adversarial callback tests cover reward, revenue, contribution, purchase, signal, and redemption paths.
Invariant campaigns require liabilities, supply, weight, and accounted balances to reconcile after every action.

protocol-time-boundaries.impact: Timestamp influence near a boundary could change an auction quote, emission epoch, deadline, or reward-stream accrual interval.
protocol-time-boundaries.exploitability: Time is the intended input to the fixed auction, daily emission, seven-day stream, and deadline state machines; proposer influence cannot bypass price bounds, epoch ordering, caps, or exact accounting.
affectedAssumptions: Robinhood Chain timestamps remain monotonic with normal Nitro sequencing behavior.
No economic rule depends on sub-block timestamp precision.
protocol-time-boundaries.revisitTrigger: Re-review if durations, deadline semantics, timestamp source, stream arithmetic, or auction price bounds change.
compensatingControls: Tests cover exact start, finish, overdue, empty-epoch, and adjacent timestamp cases.

revert-authoritative-calls.impact: Ignoring an authoritative return value could hide incomplete routing or use stale validation data.
revert-authoritative-calls.exploitability: The reported calls use typed functions whose correctness is enforced by revert and by downstream exact balance checks; their returned convenience amount is not an independent source of truth.
affectedAssumptions: The called functions continue to revert atomically on every incomplete or invalid operation.
revert-authoritative-calls.revisitTrigger: Re-review if a called ABI, return semantic, error behavior, or exact observed-delta validation changes.
compensatingControls: Tests assert both successful exact deltas and rollback for every rejected supported-token behavior.

minimal-external-administration.impact: Compromise of the Resonance setup owner or future external governance executor could change Strategy membership, reward-token registration, the prospective automatic-Bribe share, or Resonance ownership.
minimal-external-administration.exploitability: These findings identify the intended remaining administrative surface: Resonance ownership, including the globally bounded 0% through 20% prospective Bribe-share setter, plus factories and SignalGBX wired immutably to Resonance; deployment remains blocked until the exact external governance executor and its permission and upgrade model are reviewed.
affectedAssumptions: The signed deployment procedure transfers Resonance ownership to the reviewed external governance executor before protocol use and removes temporary setup authority.
setBribeBps remains owner-only, uniform across Strategies, bounded from 0 through 2,000 basis points, prospective only, and unable to reset weighted carry or reprice existing liabilities.
minimal-external-administration.revisitTrigger: Re-review when an external governance system is selected or if ownership wiring, factory callers, SignalGBX controller, Bribe-share bounds or snapshot semantics, or the Resonance administrative surface changes.
compensatingControls: Access-control and rate-transition tests enumerate privileged callers, exact bounds, prospective snapshots, and zero-rate liveness.
The release checklist blocks launch evidence until the external governance integration and ownership transfer are independently verified.

fixed-literals-and-abi-shape.impact: A mistaken fixed-point literal, ABI tuple slot, or shadowed constructor input could encode the wrong economics or position identity.
fixed-literals-and-abi-shape.exploitability: Reported numeric values are named immutable protocol constants; tuple indices match the pinned Uniswap v4 position ABI; shadowed names are explicitly qualified or isolated constructor parameters.
affectedAssumptions: Pinned emission, supply, precision, Uniswap fee, and price constants remain byte-for-byte reviewed values.
The pinned PositionManager tuple shape remains unchanged for the selected dependency version.
fixed-literals-and-abi-shape.revisitTrigger: Re-review if any constant, fixed-point unit, tuple shape, dependency version, or constructor field name changes.
compensatingControls: Constant-vector, deployment-wiring, pool-key, position-shape, and economic model tests pin the reported values.

intentional-interface-shape.impact: Unused-looking ABI parameters or public views could be removed incorrectly and break canonical interfaces or permissionless monitoring.
intentional-interface-shape.exploitability: ERC-721 receiver parameter names are retained for generated ABI documentation while authorization deliberately ignores them; public preview and custody views are composability surfaces; loop counters use Solidity zero initialization.
affectedAssumptions: IERC721Receiver selector and parameter order remain canonical.
Permissionless accounting previews and custody health views remain supported API surface.
intentional-interface-shape.revisitTrigger: Re-review if the receiver ABI, parameter authorization, public monitoring API, or zero-initialized local type changes.
compensatingControls: Interface, custody, duplicate-selection, and empty/full-loop tests cover the reported declaration shapes.
